title: A* Pathfinding (E01: algorithm explanation)
beats: Says this episode explains how A* works so later coding episodes make sense
Grid of white walkable and black obstacle nodes; goal is shortest path A to B
Picks node distance 1, diagonal sqrt2, then scales to 10 and 14 integers
Runs obstacle-free grid first; introduces G, H and F cost as corner numbers
Picks lowest F, closes it; F stays constant as G rises and H falls, so path goes straight
Adds obstacles back and reruns same procedure; F costs now climb
Ties at F 48 broken by lowest H; frontier jumps to other promising nodes
Points out a node's G cost updating when a better route is found
Concludes why it is guaranteed shortest: leaving the straight line raises F so alternatives get explored
Third run hides G/H, shows parent arrows; neighbors only repoint if the path is better
Arrows let you retrace the path from the end node
Pseudocode: open and closed lists, loop, current node, neighbor checks, parent pointers
Retrace parents back to start; says more depth comes in C# episodes

metrics.examples: 3 grid runs: empty grid, obstacles with costs shown, obstacles with arrows only; each hides more of the previous scaffolding
metrics.ending: Pseudocode walkthrough, then flat sign-off pointing to articles and later coding episodes

new_moves.name: scaffold-removal-across-reruns
new_moves.what: Each rerun hides a previously shown number and swaps in a new view, forcing the learner to use the model built earlier
new_moves.evidence: 6:01 G and H hidden, arrows shown

new_moves.name: animation-before-code
new_moves.what: Whole algorithm demonstrated visually, then pseudocode recapped while fresh
new_moves.evidence: 7:29 'while that is still fresh in your mind'

theory: The algorithm is taught as a watched execution: first the free-run case where F stays flat, then obstacles, then a third run with a different overlay. By the time pseudocode appears, every line has already been seen happening. The simplest case is also the one that gives the insight that justifies optimality.
velocity: Scene builder: author an obstacle-free run first, then the same scene with obstacles, then an overlay swap
Ghost hands: highlight the lowest-F node before it is chosen so learners predict it
Orchestrator: hold pseudocode until the learner can narrate a run
Evals: check that every code line has a prior visual referent
quote: hopefully you can see how this is guaranteed to find the shortest path
